title: Introduction to Consolidated and Separate Financial Statements
outcomes: Explain why groups prepare consolidated statements.
Map group relationships to Ind AS 110, 111, 28, 27 and 112.

meta.exam_tip: Before any consolidation, draw the group chart and label each entity with its standard.

concepts.title: Why groups prepare consolidated statements
body: Many businesses operate through several companies. Looking only at the parent's own accounts hides the assets, debts and profits sitting in subsidiaries it controls.
Consolidated statements combine the parent and its subsidiaries line by line, treating them as one economic entity, so investors and lenders see the whole group's resources and results.
Restructurings, holding company structures and tax or operational reasons often create layers of entities — making group statements essential for a fair picture.
concepts.analogy: One group, one set of numbers.
concepts.work: A parent with a thin balance sheet may control billions through subsidiaries.

concepts.title: Consolidated versus separate statements
body: Consolidated statements present the group's assets, liabilities, equity, income, expenses and cash flows as if it were a single entity, eliminating intra-group transactions and balances.

Separate statements are the parent's (or investor's) own statements, in which investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates are carried at cost, under Ind AS 109, or using the equity method.
Both may be presented; consolidated statements are not a substitute for separate statements under company law, and separate statements do not replace consolidation.
concepts.analogy: Consolidated is the group view; separate is the parent's own view.
concepts.work: Dividends from a subsidiary are income in separate accounts but eliminated in consolidated accounts.

concepts.title: The standards that make up group reporting
body: Ind AS 110 sets the control test and consolidation procedure for subsidiaries. Ind AS 111 classifies joint arrangements as joint operations or joint ventures. Ind AS 28 applies the equity method to associates and joint ventures.
Ind AS 27 governs separate financial statements. Ind AS 112 sets disclosures about interests in subsidiaries, joint arrangements, associates and unconsolidated structured entities.
Ind AS 103 covers how a subsidiary is first acquired; Ind AS 21 covers translating foreign subsidiaries.
concepts.analogy: Each relationship type has its own standard.
concepts.work: A 30% stake with board seats points to Ind AS 28.

concepts.title: Legal requirement in India
body: Under section 129(3) of the Companies Act, 2013, a company with one or more subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures must prepare consolidated financial statements in the same form and manner as its own, in addition to its standalone statements.

The Companies (Accounts) Rules provide limited exemptions, for example certain intermediate wholly owned or partly owned subsidiaries whose parent prepares consolidated statements, subject to conditions.
Listed entities must also publish consolidated results under SEBI requirements.
concepts.analogy: Law makes consolidation compulsory for most groups.
concepts.work: A listed company with one associate still prepares consolidated accounts.

mcqs.q: Consolidated statements present a group as:
mcqs.explain: Line-by-line combination. In practice: eliminate intra-group items.

mcqs.q: In separate statements, investments in subsidiaries may be measured:
options: At cost, under Ind AS 109, or by equity method
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 27 allows a choice. In practice: apply per category.

mcqs.q: The control test is found in:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 110 defines control. In practice: three elements.
mcqs.topic: The standards that make up group reporting

mcqs.q: The equity method is prescribed by:
mcqs.explain: For associates and joint ventures. In practice: one-line consolidation.
mcqs.topic: The standards that make up group reporting

mcqs.q: The Companies Act requirement for consolidated statements is in:
mcqs.explain: Applies to companies with subsidiaries, associates or JVs. In practice: rules give exemptions.
The group cannot trade with itself. In practice: also eliminate unrealised profit.

mcqs.q: Disclosures about unconsolidated structured entities are in:
mcqs.explain: Ind AS 112 covers interests in other entities. In practice: risks are disclosed.
mcqs.topic: The standards that make up group reporting

mcqs.q: Dividend from a subsidiary is, in consolidated statements:
mcqs.explain: It is an internal transfer. In practice: income in separate statements.

viva.model: Because the parent controls resources held in subsidiaries, and only a combined single-entity view shows the group's full position and results.
An entity's own statements in which investments in subsidiaries, joint ventures and associates are carried at cost, under Ind AS 109 or by the equity method.

viva.q: Which standards make up group reporting?
viva.model: Ind AS 110, 111, 28, 27 and 112, supported by Ind AS 103 and 21.
A company with subsidiaries, associates or joint ventures must also prepare consolidated statements in the same form as its own.

viva.q: What happens to intra-group transactions on consolidation?
viva.model: They are eliminated in full along with related balances and unrealised profits.

cases.title: Rana Group
cases.case: Rana Ltd. owns 100% of Sun Ltd. and 35% of Moon Ltd. (significant influence). During the year Sun paid a dividend of ₹20 crore to Rana, and Rana lent ₹50 crore to Sun.

mcqs.q: In Rana's separate statements, the dividend from Sun is:
mcqs.explain: Separate statements show it as income. In practice: eliminated in consolidation.

mcqs.q: In consolidated statements, the ₹50 crore loan is:
mcqs.explain: Intra-group balances cancel. In practice: interest also eliminated.

mcqs.q: Moon Ltd. is accounted for in consolidated statements by:
mcqs.explain: Associate under Ind AS 28. In practice: one line.
mcqs.topic: The standards that make up group reporting

mcqs.q: Rana must prepare consolidated statements because of:
mcqs.explain: It has a subsidiary and an associate. In practice: listed entities also file quarterly.
